overall: The AG found the Hinsdale Police Chief Search Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by omitting a reasonably anticipated topic (a proposed police chief job advertisement) from its March 7, 2014 notice; the committee was already disbanded, so the order was prospective only.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the committee failed to list a reasonably anticipated topic (discussion of a police chief job advertisement) in the notice for its March 7, 2014 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Members of the public could not reasonably infer from this broad topic that the discussion would include a proposed advertisement for the vacant position.

remedy: Should the Committee be reconstituted, it shall comply with the Open Meeting Law; similar future conduct may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We therefore order that, should the Committee be reconstituted, it shall comply with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar future conduct may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
